releasePlan.notes: FLAG EXISTENCE UNVERIFIED — BLOCKER: the pipeline's flag-exists-in-ld check reports that 'enable-player-login' does NOT exist in LaunchDarkly project 'default'. An earlier run said it was reused from a pr-34 run; that claim is contradicted and should not be relied on. Before releasing, the flag must be created (or confirmed) in 'default' as a multivariate string flag with variations 'control' and 'v1' (code default 'control'). Metrics: enable-player-login-error-rate (killswitch), enable-player-login-game-started (pause), enable-player-login-latency (monitoring; v1 is slower by design because players type a callsign), enable-player-login-login-completed (monitoring; fires only in v1). All on unit 'user'. Attribution caveats: (1) every anonymous visitor shares the context key 'anonymous-player', so a percentage rollout puts everyone in one group until each visitor gets their own key; (2) in v1, ldClient.identify() switches the context key to the callsign. This happens on login submit, and also in init() as soon as a callsign saved in localStorage is found. Events sent after that switch (game-started, time-to-start, late errors) are recorded against a context the flag was never evaluated for. The gate itself is evaluated once, before identify(), so it can't flip mid-session.
